newsitem.title: USA: Brent crude slips in active U.S. aftermarket.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude slips in active U.S. aftermarket.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude slipped in active cash trading in the U.S. aftermarket on Thursday, traders said.
A full boat of September Brent crude changed hands at $18.50 a barrel, but subsequent partial cargoes traded lower between $18.37 and $18.48 a barrel for a total of 700 lots.
September Brent rounded out the window at $18.35-40 a barrel, down from a settlement of $18.42 on the London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
August/September Brent traded at plus 18 cents, slightly stronger from the day's earlier trades.
September/October switched hands twice at minus five cents, even with earlier activity.
